text: In the Hill function transfer curve f(x) = alpha*x^n / (K^n + x^n) used to model a genetic part's input-output behavior, increasing the Hill coefficient n primarily makes the response...
choices: More switch-like, i.e. a steeper transition near the threshold
Leakier at zero input (higher basal expression)
Responsive at a lower half-maximal input concentration (K)
explanation: The Hill coefficient n governs the steepness and cooperativity of the transfer function: a larger n produces a sharper, more switch-like (ultrasensitive) transition around the threshold K. It does not set the maximum output level, which is the separate parameter alpha; it does not increase basal leaky expression; and it does not by itself shift the half-maximal threshold K, which is a distinct parameter from n.
